image_description: A close-up still life of several figs arranged on a white plate and a wooden surface. There are whole purple figs, halved figs revealing pink/red interiors with seeds, and one distinct yellow object that appears to be a lemon cut in half but has an anomalous texture resembling a cluster of small beads or seeds rather than typical citrus pulp.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The whole fruits exhibit the characteristic pear shape and purple/brownish coloration associated with ripe figs.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Smooth to slightly wrinkled texture with matte finish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin of the whole figs appears smooth with a natural matte sheen, consistent with real figs.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The geometry of the whole fruits correctly tapers from the base to the stem.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Narrow stem end contrasting with broad rounded base.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Sweet, pink to amber-colored fleshy pulp surrounding seeds.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The interior color gradient from red/pink near the skin to lighter center is accurate for this variety.
The visual rendering of the cut surface suggests a moist, soft texture rather than a dry or fibrous one.

artifact_observations.location: Right side of image, yellow cut fruit
artifact_observations.reasoning: The yellow object (likely intended to be a lemon or yellow fig) has a highly unnatural texture. Instead of citrus segments or fig pulp, it appears as a uniform grid of raised yellow beads or spheres. This is a significant structural/textural hallucination.
The wood grain lines in the background warp and bend unnaturally around the plate, suggesting a slight depth/geometry error in the background generation.
